author: SamitHuang
body:
They operate at two different layers of the lifecycle and protect against different failure modes:
  ```text
  [ Worker Process ]                                    [ Engine / Client Process ]
  Worker finishes forward pass
     │
     ├──> Enqueues D2H/SHM task to background thread
     │    and sends COMPUTE_DONE ──────────────────────> Engine waits for OUTPUT_READY
     │                                                   (deadline: _ASYNC_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT = 30.0s)
     │
  Trainer/Engine invokes sleep/wake or memory release
     │
  Worker calls drain_async_outputs()
  (deadline: _ASYNC_OUTPUT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S = 10.0s)
     │
     ├── Background thread finishes D2H/SHM (~10-50 ms)
     └── Worker safely releases GPU memory
  ```
  | Parameter | Location | Scope & Role |
  | :--- | :--- | :--- |
  | **`_ASYNC_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT`** (`30.0s`) | **Engine** (`diffusion_engine.py`) | Total deadline for the engine/client to receive `OUTPUT_READY` (D2H transfer + SHM write + queue
  delivery) after compute finishes. |
  | **`_ASYNC_OUTPUT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S`** (`10.0s`) | **Worker** (`diffusion_worker.py`) | Barrier timeout when a worker is asked to sleep or release device memory. It waits for
  already-enqueued background D2H/SHM tasks to finish so GPU tensors aren't freed while being read. |
  ### Why `_ASYNC_OUTPUT_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S` is set to 10.0s:
  1. **Draining is fast**: Draining only waits for in-flight D2H memory copies and POSIX SHM writes, which typically complete in under 50–100 ms.
  2. **Preventing timeout inversion**: If drain timeout were 60.0s (larger than the engine's 30.0s), a wedged worker background thread could hold the sleep RPC for 60s while the
  engine already timed out at 30s, causing desynchronized aborts across processes. Keeping drain timeout at **10.0s** guarantees worker memory barriers complete well within the
  engine's 30.0s wait window.
